title: A Slate Under the Jar
author: a pilgrim, in chalk; and someone else, after
body:
# Under the jar on Isse's stone

*A roof-slate, written on in chalk, and the chalk run where the jar has stood on it wet.*

---

I brought water from the Wellspring down the stair, as the Sayers' book says the Builders did once a year, so that the cistern would remember what it is for. I poured it in the tank. It was dry. It went into the stone and was gone.

I left the jar full on the stone for Isse, who taught the stilts and knows about water standing where it should not.

*Under it, in another hand, in the same chalk, wet:*

It remembers.

Is it still water?
